replacement: Dropped Nov 10, 2026 (too in depth, owner): the estimate stays as the game's answer. Was: Coefficients checked against P9 life replays and real bereaved/harmed-cohort spreads of civic action.

whatItFakes: Drive formation's responses to bereavement and layoff are calibrated to published bands; the cause, guard and calling fits for every other event, the trait-lean gain and the illness, crime and injustice responses are still prototype values.
why: Event-born drives were zero in P8 (acceptance d); the decision path is real but its response set and weights are uncalibrated.
replacement: Dropped Nov 10, 2026 (too in depth, owner): the estimate stays as the game's answer. Was: Researched Oct 24, 2026: the band the response pressures calibrate against is data/research/people/trauma-trajectories-2018.json (Galatzer-Levy, Huang and Bonanno, Clinical Psychology Review 2018: 65.7% resilient after a potential trauma, 95% interval 61.6 to 69.8), reported against the town's bereavement carry-on share by scripts/research/people-year.ts; the builder item people-drives-responses-against-research-bands sets the pressures. Response rows and pressures calibrated against documented responses to bereavement, job loss and injustice (P9 lives, panel studies). Calibrated Oct 24, 2026 (traits lead): the bereavement rules carry their own drive-fit multiple (responseBereavementFitScale 2.1) and the grudge fit is 1.7, so about two in three of the bereaved who can form a drive of their own carry on and 1.7 to 14.9% of the laid off hold a grudge (data/research/people/termination-claims-1998.json); the cause, guard and calling fits for every other event, the trait-lean gain and the illness, crime and injustice responses are still prototype values with no band.
resolvedBy: stand-in triage T9 (owner, Nov 10: too in depth)

whatItFakes: Trait-weighted perception channels (loss, others' distress, injustice, threat, persuasion) choosing which traits raise or lower an event's weight; channel membership is authored.
why: The owner approved bounded perception; no source maps these traits to event salience yet.
replacement: Dropped Nov 10, 2026 (too in depth, owner): the estimate stays as the game's answer. Was: Researched Oct 24, 2026: no appraisal study with a trait-to-salience effect that converts to a channel weight was found (Europe PMC searches for a pooled neuroticism and perceived-stress or stress-reactivity estimate returned single studies only), so channel rows stay authored; the builder item people-drives-responses-against-research-bands starts with that search. Channel rows and weights validated against appraisal research and P9 replays. Oct 24, 2026 (traits lead): the injustice channel's directions (forgiving lowers, vindictive and defensive raise) agree in sign with the forgiveness meta-analysis (data/research/people/fehr-forgiveness-correlates-2010.json: trait forgiveness r = .30, agreeableness .22, neuroticism -.24, trait anger -.18 with forgiving an offender); the loss, others'-distress, threat and persuasion channels still have no study.
resolvedBy: stand-in triage T9 (owner, Nov 10: too in depth)

whatItFakes: A resident founds a cause group instantly with no charter, registration, dues or officers.
why: Organizing needs a place for others to join; the nonprofit and association engine is not built.
replacement: An association engine with formation steps, registration law per place and membership rules.
resolution: Founding stays one act on a recorded drive (the found-cause-group act in src/core2/data/drives.json): the standing rule 'This is a game, not a spreadsheet' in AGENTS.md admits no charter, registration or dues step the golden path does not need and The Political Process does not have. The group's depth is where it reacts: the members who join and what the interest-groups engine does with it.

whatItFakes: Testifying at a hearing is a registered act row that is never offered.
why: Core2 has no hearings or legislature.
replacement: The legislature/committee module's hearing calendar offering testimony slots.
resolution: the act row is deleted. Testimony is a resident's remark at a hearing or meeting (the meetings module's remarks and hearings), chosen from the resident's own views, so a second drive act would be a parallel route.

whatItFakes: Running for office is a registered act row that is never offered.
why: Core2 has no elections or filing.
replacement: The elections module's filing and campaign acts.
resolution: the act row is deleted. Who runs is decided by the elections and candidacy modules (candidacy.ts, candidate-pool.ts, world-races), so a drive act would be a parallel route.

whatItFakes: Lobbying a legislator is a registered act row that is never offered.
why: Core2 has no legislature or member contact system.
replacement: The legislature module's member-contact and bill-sponsor acts.
resolution: the act row is deleted. Lobbying is the interest-groups module's contact with a legislator, so a drive act would be a parallel route.
